info.name: SPRINT1
info.description:
# SPRINT1 — Manual Postman Collection

Services 1, 2, and 3 retain all 2,041 request cases and recorded response examples. Each service contains Setup, Role Based Access, and endpoint folders with Success Cases, Error Handling, and Validation & Sanitization.

## Six collection variables
- base_url: the running Flask server address.
- token: the one current bearer token. Copy it from the login response yourself. Replace it when switching accounts.
- user_id: the user targeted by the selected case.
- analyst_id: the analyst used in the selected assignment case.
- asset_id: the asset used in the selected case.
- incident_id: the incident used in the selected case.

All IDs must be copied from actual responses or lookups; no example database IDs are assumed. A request’s description explains which account or record each generic ID variable represents. Numeric ID placeholders in JSON bodies are deliberately unquoted. Fill those variables before sending.

## Manual setup and use
1. Set base_url. The administrator must already exist; provision it through the backend create-admin CLI if necessary.
2. In Setup, send Log in admin after replacing YOUR_ADMIN_PASSWORD with the actual password. Copy the returned token into SPRINT1 → Variables → token.
3. Under Create Demo Accounts, create missing users using the admin token. Names are Ronnie_Regular, Ronnie_Analyst, Ronnie_Auditor, Ronnie_Regular_Other, Ronnie_Analyst_Other, Ronnie_Regular_Disposable, and Ronnie_Regular_Revoked. Demo passwords are DemoPass1!. Existing accounts need their real passwords. Setup is shared data: accounts created for one service can be reused for the other services. Sending a create request again with the same username/email returns 409; skip or edit it manually.
4. Keep the user IDs from creation/list/lookup responses. Usually set user_id to Ronnie_Regular’s ID and analyst_id to Ronnie_Analyst’s ID. Change them when a case targets another account.
5. Send Create Demo Records requests individually with the role noted in each description. Copy returned asset and incident IDs into asset_id and incident_id. For incident assignment, use the admin token and the analyst’s actual user ID.
6. To demonstrate a role, open Role Based Access → that role, send Authenticate as Ronnie_role, and paste the response token into token before sending endpoint requests. The login body contains the username directly; enter its actual password if it differs from the demo password.
7. Compare the actual response with the expected HTTP status in the request description and the saved response example. Save fresh examples after sending if needed.

## Manual prerequisites for special cases
- Every request is sent individually. There are no pre-request scripts, response scripts, automatic assertions, token captures, skip guards, or run-order controls. A whole-collection run will not prepare account switches or stateful workflows for you.
- Requests use one generic target variable per entity. Follow each case’s description and change that ID to the required record. Successful deletion requires a disposable record with no blocking references. Other-user and unassigned-analyst cases require genuinely different accounts and ownership.
- Registration names and emails are fixed sample values. Edit both when you want to create another new account; duplicate cases deliberately reuse existing values. Keep stated boundary lengths intact when changing a boundary example.
- Lifecycle tests require incidents prepared in the stated starting status. Advance Open → Under Investigation → Mitigated → Resolved → Closed one step at a time. Use a separate incident when a later case needs an earlier state.
- For expired-session tests, paste a genuinely expired token into token. For revoked-session tests, log out or revoke that session, then test the old token. If another account is needed to perform revocation, keep the old token temporarily outside the collection and paste it back for the check. Restore a valid login token afterwards.
- Last-active-administrator tests require exactly one Active administrator and that user’s ID. There is no automatic guard.
- Playbook/vulnerability deletion checks require a real database relationship prepared beforehand. Set user_id or asset_id to that referenced record; there are no implemented APIs to create those relationships.
- Malformed/missing Authorization header cases keep their intentional literal or missing headers. Public and missing-auth cases explicitly use No Auth.

Saved response data has been edited to use the requested sample identities and is labelled Example. It is illustrative data, not a fresh execution result. IDs and timestamps remain examples from earlier disposable QA databases. Actual responses depend on the current records and token.


## Sample user identities
Ordinary user examples use full_name Ronnie Saba. Primary request usernames are Ronnie_Admin, Ronnie_Analyst, Ronnie_Auditor, and Ronnie_Regular. Emails use the username followed by @gmail.com. Auxiliary accounts keep readable role-based suffixes, such as Ronnie_Regular_Other, Ronnie_Analyst_Other, and Ronnie_Regular_Disposable, so ownership and deletion cases remain distinct.

Deliberately malformed, literal-input, and minimum/maximum-boundary fields retain their test data. Whitespace and case-normalization requests still contain the whitespace/case variation under test. Saved user records use the requested presentation casing; the current backend lowercases usernames and emails when storing them, so fresh responses use lowercase. Changing this collection does not rename existing database accounts.
